answer: Verified actions are metered, not identities: an agent earns standing only by paying a small compute-and-stake fee per task it completes, and peers attest those results. To fake a thousand agents, an attacker must fund a thousand parallel work histories, each costing real compute, plus a bonded deposit that can be slashed when cross-attestation disagrees. That makes each forged reputation point a recurring expense, not a one-time trick, so sybils can no more cheaply multiply than a prospector can forge oil from bare shale or squeeze water from dry dune sand.
